name: Kulfi Faluda
instructions: 1. Boil milk in a heavy-bottomed pan and simmer until reduced to half its volume, stirring constantly to prevent burning.
2. Add sugar, cardamom powder, and saffron strands, cooking until the mixture thickens into a rabri consistency.
3. Cool the mixture, pour into kulfi molds, and freeze until set solid.
4. Prepare the falooda sev by boiling in water, then immediately rinsing in cold water to separate strands.
5. Soak sabja seeds in water until they swell.
6. To serve, place a portion of chilled falooda sev and soaked seeds in a bowl or glass, add the unmolded kulfi, and drizzle generously with rose syrup and nuts.
description: Kulfi Faluda is an iconic street food of Uttar Pradesh, particularly famous in Lucknow and Varanasi. It represents the rich Mughal culinary heritage, offering a perfect balance of the creamy, nutty frozen kulfi and the cooling, textural contrast of vermicelli and rose-scented syrup, often enjoyed as a refreshing treat during hot summer evenings.
